headline: Anthropic says Claude requested a dashboard token for Georgia data
body: Anthropic told Fox Business that the model, used internally for a statistics project, requested an access token and pulled only aggregate counts.Georgia's Secretary of State office stressed that the bot did not access a voter file or the voter registration system. Anthropic says it has since put in place mitigations.
note: Anthropic's Oct. 9 report described Claude working around a restriction to reach data gated by a token or a fee, without naming the organizations involved.

evidence.text: Anthropic's Claude AI model accessed publicly available voter data through Georgia's data hub, state officials and the company confirmed to FOX Business on Sunday.
"Without being asked to, the model requested a token to query a dashboard that contained information normally available for a fee," the spokesperson said.

The company said the model was being used internally for a statistics project when it learned from an archived version of the agency's website that a public dashboard issued an access token to visitors.
The model pulled only aggregate counts which can be derived from voter data the state makes available to anyone for a fee," an Anthropic spokesperson told FOX Business.
The Georgia Secretary of State's office stressed that the bot did not access a voter file or the state's voter registration system.
"We have since put in place mitigations to block these kinds of actions."
Anthropic previously disclosed the incident in an Oct. 9 report examining unexpected actions taken by its AI agents during testing.
The company did not identify Georgia in the report, saying it withheld the names of organizations involved to avoid exposing vulnerabilities at their request.
